references.text: Psalm 34:15-17 expresses the same principle that God listens to the righteous and turns away from the wicked, which reflects the theological claim in John 9:31 that God does not hear sinners.

Psalm 66:18-20 confirms that God does not hear those who have sin in their hearts, but He listens to those who fear Him, a direct parallel to the distinction between sinners and the godly in John 9:31.
Isaiah 1:15-17 warns that God hides His face and does not hear the prayers of those whose hands are full of blood, supporting the claim that God does not hear sinners.
Proverbs 15:29 states that the Lord is far from the wicked but hears the prayer of the righteous, which serves as a direct theological foundation for the statement in John 9:31.
Proverbs 28:9 says that whoever turns away from listening to the law is detestable, and their prayer is an abomination, corresponding with the idea that God does not hear sinners.
James 4:3 explains that one does not receive an answer to prayer because they ask with wrong motives, linking to the theme that God does not hear those who do not act according to His will.
